fields.aka: Jagadbandhu Sundara, Jagadvandhu Sundara Prabhu, Prabhu Jagadbandhu, Bandhu
fields.appearance: Sītā-navamī, 17 Vaiśākha 1871, at Dāhāpāḍā (Murshidabad) (the record's text)
fields.disappearance: 1 Āśvina 1328 BS (1921) (record of Atula Campati; his own texts say 1931, a misprint)
fields.place: Born at Dāhāpāḍā (Murshidabad); Faridpur (Brahmankāṇḍā, Bākcara, Goālcāmaṭ 1902–1918); Pabna; Calcutta (Rāmbāgān, Cāsādhopāpāḍā); Navadvīpa
fields.disciples: Atula Candra Campati, Rādhikā Gupta (Rāmadāsa Bābājī), Pratāpa Bhaumika, Rameśa Cakravartī, Jayanitāi (Devena Cakravartī), Tārakā Gāṅgulī, Dr Uṣā Majumdar, Navadvīpa dāsa; Rajanī Bāgdi («Haridāsa Pāśa», the Mahānta-sampradāya)
fields.works: Candrapāṭa, Hari-kathā, Śrīmatī-saṅkīrtana, Śrī Śrī Nāma-saṅkīrtana, Vividha-saṅgīta, Padāvalī, Trikāla-grantha
fields.notes: Son of Dīnanātha Nyāyaratna and Vāmāsundarī; brought up by his uncle Bhairava Cakravartī at Faridpur. Led a great nāma-saṅkīrtana movement in Bengal among the outcast and low-caste (the Ḍoms of Calcutta, the Bāgdis, tribal people of Jessore and Khulna); lived long in mauna. Not the Jagadbandhu Prabhu of Advaita's family (record of Gaura Kiśora Śiromaṇi).

fields.name: Atula Candra Campati (Calcutta)
fields.aka: Atula Candrā Champati (Calcutta), Atulachandra Champati, Campati Mahāśaya
fields.place: Calcutta (1 Madan Mitra Lane); Arrah (headmaster); Pabna; Goālcāmaṭ (Faridpur)
fields.guru: Prabhu Jagadbandhu Sundara (his wife's maternal uncle); blessed by Haraṇa Kṣepā of Pabna
fields.notes: A B.A. with honours and headmaster at Arrah; married Kṣīrodā, niece of Jagadbandhu, whose most ecstatic devotee he became after a sign on the railway line. Wandered Calcutta in kīrtana, begging among outcasts and prostitutes; supervised the service at Goālcāmaṭ; friend of Vipina Bihārī Caṭṭopādhyāya, who died in his lap. Known personally to Haridāsa dāsa, who wrote his life. Died 1925.

fields.place: Born in Mahārāṣṭra; Puṣkara, Kurukṣetra; Amritsar, Jammu, Lahore (Punjab)
fields.guru: A sannyāsī from Tailaṅga-deśa, Vaiṣṇava of the «Kuver» sect (sannyāsa at Puṣkara)
fields.notes: A famous yogī of the early 19th century, who stayed alive buried in samādhi for weeks and months (Amritsar, Jammu, before McNaughton at Puṣkara, Lahore 1835 before Ranjit Siṁha); not of the Gauḍīya line (Viśvakoṣa vol. 22).
